name: Bolasterone (Finaject)
lead: Bolasterone, chemically 7-alpha,17-alpha-dimethyltestosterone, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid developed by the Upjohn Company for veterinary use. Anabolic steroids as a class are used by some bodybuilders and physique athletes in pursuit of greater muscle mass, and bolasterone belongs to that family, though it is little known in current looksmaxxing and bodybuilding discussion [6][1]. Its 17-alpha-methyl group improves oral bioavailability and its 7-alpha-methyl group is shared with its isomer calusterone [1].

It is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency and is listed as a controlled anabolic steroid in Brazil [1]. Wikipedia notes an unreferenced claim that East German authorities obtained it for athletes through the state sports-medicine research institute [1].

Little published material covers bolasterone. Most of the scientific literature that mentions it concerns detection chemistry in doping control, including recent metabolism studies in rat liver microsomes and rat urine, and no clinical trials in people were found [2][4][5].

paras: Bolasterone is a testosterone derivative with methyl groups at positions 7 and 17. It is described as having a low-to-moderate ratio of anabolic to androgenic activity, comparable to fluoxymesterone [1].

Published pharmacology is largely analytical. A 2023 study identified 16 hydroxylated metabolites plus a reduced metabolite and a glucuronide conjugate after oral administration in rats and rat liver microsomes [4]. A 2025 study using gas chromatography tandem mass spectrometry reported 12 hydroxylated metabolites and proposed structures for them, to help anti-doping laboratories detect use [5].

No studies found. The published literature touching on bolasterone is analytical: for example, work on how 17-methyl steroids including bolasterone are epimerised and excreted in humans [2], metabolite identification in rats [4][5], and methods for detecting anabolic steroids in urine and horse samples [3].

Wikipedia lists the brand names Myagen and Methosarb and the developmental code U-19763 [1]. Because it is detected in anti-doping and horse-racing screens [3], it appears in the testing literature. It has no established place in modern looksmaxxing or bodybuilding discussion.

A 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders in Kansas and Missouri reported that 54 percent of men used steroids regularly and listed products used, including one named Finaject, among many others; that survey did not describe bolasterone [6].

card.summary: An obscure Upjohn-era veterinary oral steroid, now mostly a name in anti-doping detection papers.

quick.overview:
Bolasterone is an oral anabolic steroid made by Upjohn for veterinary use. It is banned in sport.

Very little has been published about it beyond detection methods, so there is no human evidence for appearance or muscle effects.
quick.mechanism: It is a methylated testosterone analog; the 17-methyl group lets it work when swallowed. Its anabolic-to-androgenic ratio is described as low to moderate.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. Risks are inferred from other 17-alkylated oral steroids. It is prohibited by WADA and controlled in some countries such as Brazil.

chain: Androgen receptor activation promotes muscle growth
angle.text: As an androgen, bolasterone is the kind of compound athletes have used with the aim of adding muscle, and a more muscular build is how it would affect appearance. No human studies describe its effect on physique.
